title: hello-federation — the smoke is the demo (the one starter with no crewhaus.yaml)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “This directory is intentionally light.” The only starter with no spec — and that's the point.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — for symmetry with every other drive. Nothing in this one actually needs a key.

verify.note: operator-supplied demos/.env. Nothing below needs a key — the smoke is hermetic and `federation discover` is a deliberate connection failure.

groups.title: Beat 1 · There is no spec to type

beats.label: Open the smoke instead
beats.cue: “No crewhaus.yaml to compile — the runtime lives in the deployments.” Six probes stand in.

beats.label: Find the three packages
beats.cue: Protocol, discovery, router — federation is composed in code. There is no spec.federation block.

beats.label: Run the federation smoke
beats.cue: “No docker required, no live cross-host call.” Fourteen checks, end to end, all green.

verify.note: 14 ✓ checks across probes A–E; probe F is skipped without CREWHAUS_FEDERATION_LIVE=1. Contributor path — needs the sibling ../factory checkout: demos declares no @crewhaus dependency, so the three federation imports resolve through tsconfig.json's `"@crewhaus/*": ["../factory/packages/*"]`, and smoke.ts:105 readFileSync's probe C's mTLS fixtures straight out of ../factory/packages/federation-protocol/src. Without that sibling the beat exits 1. `bun run smoke:section-34` resolves from the root package.json, so it runs fine from this starter dir.

beats.label: Ask the CLI to find a peer
beats.cue: Discovery is the CLI's one federation verb — point it at a peer that isn't there and it fails closed.

verify.note: deliberate rejection — deployment-b.example is the smoke's fixture peer, not a real host: `federation discover: peer discovery failed`

beats.label: Read the error taxonomy
beats.cue: ECONNREFUSED retries, a 503 retries — but a cert-pin mismatch tombstones the peer.

verify.note: probe D — 4 assertions over the retry / tombstone / fail taxonomy, plus the import

groups.title: One more thing · how production wires peers

beats.label: Show both sides of a federated call
beats.cue: The caller builds a router and calls; the callee decodes the envelope and runs the named role.

verify.note: 8 matching lines — the exact three calls the README's "How production wires peers" names

beats.label: Open walkthrough 27
beats.cue: The envelope shape, mTLS pinning, traceparent propagation, error classification — in full.
